how_to_apply: Fill in the application in the prescribed format given as Annexure-I ("Application for the Post of Consultant at National Defence College, New Delhi") in the notice.
Paste a recent passport size photograph on the form.
Enclose the copies the form asks for (listed below).
Sign the declaration on the form with place, date and full name.
Send the duly completed form by registered mail or by hand, addressed to The Commandant, National Defence College, 6 - Tees January Marg, New Delhi – 110011.

The form should be sent within 21 days of the publication of the notification; the last date of application is printed as 28 November 2026, and paragraph 2 of the detailed advertisement says up to 20 November 2026.
Copy of education/technical qualification certificate/mark sheet
Brief particulars of experience of the last 10 years (assignment-wise) – a separate sheet may be annexed

The form also asks for date of birth, contact details, address for communication, date of joining government service, age, whether SC/ST/OBC, whether physically handicapped, the Ministry/Department/Organisation from which retired, and details of computer knowledge.

content_sections.heading: About NDC
content_sections.text: The National Defence College is located at 6 - Tees January Marg, New Delhi and functions under the Ministry of Defence, Government of India. The Consultant (SME) will support the NDC course, and according to the Terms of Reference the Consultant engaged at NDC would be working as Senior Directing Staff for all practical purposes.

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: Qualification: NDC course or equivalent, with expertise in National Security & Strategies. Profile: The candidate must be a practitioner-scholar with preferably a PhD degree, an outstanding professional record within national security establishments, and a distinguished academic and publishing record. Additional qualifying requirements: Necessary teaching and research assignments in India and/or abroad. Knowledge and ability: Candidates would need to demonstrate a sound knowledge of the national security system and possess the ability to suitably mentor operational practitioners undergoing the NDC course. Age limit: Age of the candidate should not be more than 65 years as on 31 December 2027. The notice does not mention any age relaxation. For the full eligibility conditions of the post, candidates should check the official notification.

content_sections.heading: Pay and Tenure
content_sections.text: The maximum monthly remuneration of the Consultant (SME), depending upon pay level, is Rs 65,000/- (Rupees Sixty-Five Thousand only) to Rs. 80,000/- (Rupees Eighty Thousand only). TDS as admissible will be deducted from the monthly remuneration, and the concerned Drawing and Disbursing Officer will issue a TDS certificate on demand.

content_sections.heading: NDC Consultant (SME) Job Description
content_sections.text: Under the Terms of Reference (Annexure-II), the Consultant (SME) would be expected to carry out the following minimum tasks: Conduct Integrated Analysis Group (IAG) meetings. Conduct one of the modules as assigned by the College. Guide the Course Members (up to a maximum of 18 members) assigned to him/her in selection of topics, completion of thesis and their internal evaluation/assessment, including viva voce. Attend selected lectures, panel discussions and presentations conducted as part of training activity and promulgated in the weekly training programme of NDC. Assess all written assignments submitted by the assigned Course Members, including recommendation for publication in NDC Journal. Supervise presentations given by the assigned Course Members. Attend all faculty meetings and other deliberations organised in connection with running of the NDC course. Tasks are to be completed as per the published Block Calendar and weekly training programme for the current NDC course.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for NDC Consultant (SME)
content_sections.text: Recent passport size photograph Copy of retirement order Copy of last pay drawn Copy of education/technical qualification certificate/mark sheet Copy of PPO Brief particulars of experience of the last 10 years (assignment-wise) – a separate sheet may be annexed The form also asks for date of birth, contact details, address for communication, date of joining government service, age, whether SC/ST/OBC, whether physically handicapped, the Ministry/Department/Organisation from which retired, and details of computer knowledge.

content_sections.heading: Selection and Interview
content_sections.text: Applications completed in all respects will be screened by a Screening-cum-Selection Committee of three members: the Commandant, NDC (Chairman), the Senior most Senior Directing Staff, NDC (Member) and the Secretary, NDC (Member). The Committee shall hold a personal interaction with the shortlisted candidates, if required. Selection would be purely on merit in accordance with qualification and experience, and the decision of the Committee is final. The selected candidate will receive an offer letter with the terms and conditions of engagement, and no Consultant (SME) is allowed to join without first submitting an undertaking accepting those terms.

faq.question: Q1. How many vacancies are there in NDC Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: There is one post of Consultant (Subject Matter Expert) at National Defence College, New Delhi.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date for the NDC Consultant (SME) application?
faq.answer: The last date of application is 28 November 2026; paragraph 2 of the detailed advertisement says applications may be sent up to 20 November 2026.

faq.question: Q3. What qualification is required for NDC Consultant (SME)?
faq.answer: The qualification is the NDC course or equivalent, with expertise in National Security & Strategies; the candidate must be a practitioner-scholar with preferably a PhD degree and an outstanding record within national security establishments.

faq.question: Q4. What is the age limit for the NDC Consultant (SME) post?
faq.answer: Age of the candidate should not be more than 65 years as on 31 December 2027.

faq.question: Q5. What is the salary of NDC Consultant (SME)?
faq.answer: The remuneration is Rs 65,000/- to Rs. 80,000/- per month, depending upon pay level, with no allowances or accommodation facility.

faq.question: Q6. How do I apply for the NDC Consultant (SME) post?
faq.answer: Send the Annexure-I form with the required copies by registered mail or by hand to The Commandant, National Defence College, 6 - Tees January Marg, New Delhi – 110011.

faq.question: Q7. How will the NDC Consultant (SME) be selected?
faq.answer: A three-member Screening-cum-Selection Committee will screen applications and hold a personal interaction with shortlisted candidates, if required; selection is purely on merit in accordance with qualification and experience.

faq.question: Q8. Is the NDC Consultant (SME) job permanent?
faq.answer: No. The engagement is full-time and of a temporary (non-official) nature for 12 months (01 January 2027 to 31 December 2027, extendable for another 12 months), with no absorption or regularisation of service with NDC.

faq.question: Q9. Can a retired government official keep drawing pension as NDC Consultant (SME)?
faq.answer: Yes. A retired Government official appointed as Consultant (SME) continues to draw pension and dearness relief on pension, and the engagement is not treated as re-employment.

faq.question: Q10. How much leave does an NDC Consultant (SME) get?
faq.answer: The Consultant (SME) is eligible for eight (08) days of leave in a calendar year on pro-rata basis; un-availed leave is neither carried forward nor encashed.
